description: Verify that TCP in FIN-WAIT-1 sends an ACK with next expected SEQ after receiving any segment with OTW SEQ number (RFC 793 §3.9 p69). 5 iterations exercise flag set ∈ {SYN, SYN+ACK, ACK, FIN, data}
approach:
[Objective]
Out-of-window (OTW) SEQ means the seg.seq is outside the receive window. RFC 793 §3.9 mandates DUT reply with an ACK announcing the SEQ it actually expects — so the peer can resync. The flag set on the OTW segment doesn't matter (SYN, ACK, FIN, data — same response).

[Scenario — chronological]
For each phase (per flag set), DUT is driven to FIN-WAIT-1 (DUT FIN must precede), then tester injects an OTW-SEQ segment with that phase's flags. DUT must reply with the proper-SEQ ACK.

[Pass condition]
All phases observe the correct probe ACK.

[Fail condition]
Per-phase: Fail_p<n>_no_handshake_ack / Fail_p<n>_no_probe_ack.

verdicts.Pass: DUT acked OTW-SEQ probe in all flag-variant phases — normal
verdicts.Fail_p1_no_dut_fin: No DUT no dut fin phase 1
verdicts.Fail_p1_no_probe_ack: No DUT ACK to OTW-SEQ probe phase 1
verdicts.Fail_p2_no_dut_fin: No DUT no dut fin phase 2
verdicts.Fail_p2_no_probe_ack: No DUT ACK to OTW-SEQ probe phase 2

verdicts.Fail_p3_no_probe_ack: No DUT ACK to OTW-SEQ probe phase 3
verdicts.Fail_p4_no_dut_fin: No DUT no dut fin phase 4
verdicts.Fail_p4_no_probe_ack: No DUT ACK to OTW-SEQ probe phase 4
